deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a section titled roughly 'Inégalités de convexité et classes remarquables d'opérateurs'. Its purpose is to build the convexity machinery needed to compare symmetric functions of eigenvalues with the same functions of singular values ('s-numbers') of compact operators. That comparison is what lets one define and handle symmetric-norm operator ideals such as the Schatten classes.

Theorem 1 (1°), attributed to H. Weyl.
- Let (α_i) and (β_i), i ≤ n, be finite real sequences with α_1 ≥ … ≥ α_n.
- Assume weak submajorization: α_1+…+α_m ≤ β_1+…+β_m for m = 1,…,n.
- Let φ be a convex symmetric function on R^n.
- Assume either (a) φ is increasing in each argument, or (b) Σα_i = Σβ_i, i.e. majorization.
- Then φ(α) ≤ φ(β).

This is the Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya / Karamata / Tomić–Weyl majorization inequality. Only the α are assumed ordered. The β need not be: replacing β by its decreasing rearrangement only increases the partial sums and leaves φ(β) unchanged by symmetry.

Corollary (2°), the multiplicative form.
- Let f be symmetric in n arguments t_i ≥ 0, with t ↦ f(e^{t_1},…,e^{t_n}) convex on R^n.
- Let ρ_1 ≥ … ≥ ρ_n ≥ 0 and σ_i ≥ 0 satisfy ρ_1⋯ρ_m ≤ σ_1⋯σ_m for all m.
- Assume either (a) f is increasing in each argument and continuous on t_i ≥ 0, or (b) ρ_1⋯ρ_n = σ_1⋯σ_n ≠ 0.
- Then f(ρ) ≤ f(σ).

Proof of the corollary.
- For strictly positive entries, set α_i = log ρ_i and β_i = log σ_i and apply the theorem. This already settles case (b), where all entries are nonzero.
- In case (a), every admissible system with zeros is approximated in R^{2n} by admissible systems with ρ'_i, σ'_i > 0. One makes the σ_i positive and raises the vanishing ρ_i slightly while keeping the product inequalities. Continuity of f then gives the result in the limit.
- The approximation is fiddled with at the bottom of this page and on the next page, through the cases σ_n > 0 and σ_{n-1} > 0 = σ_n.

Proof of the theorem (previous and next pages). A convex φ is the supremum of affine minorants L_k. If φ is increasing, these L_k have nonnegative linear coefficients. One then reduces to linear functions, where the Abel-summation argument applies.

The intended application is Weyl's 1949 inequality Π|λ_i| ≤ Π s_i, which via the corollary yields Σ g(|λ_i|) ≤ Σ g(s_i) for suitable g, e.g. Σ|λ_i|^p ≤ Σ s_i^p.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible in the statements; they are correct as given, including the observation that only (α_i) or (ρ_i) needs to be ordered.

The zero-approximation argument in case (a) of 2° is left messy and unfinished on this page and continued, with several crossed-out attempts, on the next page. It is a minor technical gap, not an error.

ideas.what: Convex symmetric (increasing) φ is monotone under (weak) majorization, with only one sequence ordered
ideas.modern_name: Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya–Karamata majorization inequality / Tomić–Weyl weak majorization theorem
ideas.where_published: Probably used in Grothendieck's Bourbaki seminar exposé on rearrangements and convexity inequalities in von Neumann algebras with trace (1955), and possibly in Produits tensoriels topologiques (1955); unsure of the exact formulation there

ideas.what: Multiplicative version: f(e^t) convex and products of the ρ dominated by products of the σ imply f(ρ) ≤ f(σ), with zeros handled by approximation
ideas.modern_name: Weyl's multiplicative majorization lemma (log-majorization), applied to eigenvalues versus singular values

ideas.what: Increasing convex function as the supremum of affine functions with nonnegative coefficients (supporting hyperplanes)
ideas.modern_name: Supporting hyperplane / subgradient characterization of monotone convex functions

deep.surprise_reason: This is Grothendieck carefully re-deriving Weyl's 1949 majorization inequalities, which were standard by then, as groundwork for operator classes defined by s-numbers. The statements are classical and correctly credited to Weyl on the page itself. The only personal touches are minor technical care: ordering only one sequence, and handling zero entries by approximation.
transcription_corrections: The circled label at the top reads '(Th. 1)' rather than '(Lemme 1)'. This is consistent with the later 'énoncé du th.', where 'lemme' is crossed out.
The label '(2°)' in the line 'Cela prouve (2°) … dans le cas b)' is likely correct, i.e. 'Cela prouve 2° dans le cas b)'. The positive-entries argument covers case (b) fully.

Left margins contain circled marginal notes, apparently beginning 'Il suffit …' / 'En fait …' and perhaps saying that only one sequence needs ordering. They are not transcribed and are largely illegible.
The bracketed '(2)' and '(1)' labels on the hypotheses correspond to circled numerals on the image; the partial-sum condition is circled as ② and the ordering condition as (1).
